summary:
PULSE is a web-based astronaut health monitoring system that helps crews gather, evaluate, and act when Earth medical support is unavailable. It addresses the NASA Space Apps health-monitoring challenge by combining a live mission dashboard (vitals, radiation, cabin CO₂, sleep, behavioral check-ins) with offline local AI that only proposes citation-backed procedures from NASA HRP / CSA-style standing orders.

When a solar flare causes HF radio blackout or on a Mars path during solar conjunction the Earth link drops to LOS. PULSE switches to local AI: it states what happened to the crewmember, a hypothesized reason, and whether citations support that reason (supported / partial / not confirmed). A second crewmate applies the steps; vitals normalize; AOS restores and receipts sync.

This matters because spacecraft seats are too costly to always fly a physician, and distance from Earth is a core HRP hazard. PULSE keeps the crew from going medically “blind” when the radio dies. Simulated demo data only not a medical device.
details:
PULSE is a Next.js mission health floor for deep-space crews that gathers multi-channel telemetry (HR, SpO₂, temperature, blood pressure, personal radiation dose, cabin CO₂, sleep, mood), evaluates samples with receipted engines and a BLIND quality gate, and supports action through citation-backed standing-order interventions when Earth surgeons are offline—running a live crew dashboard and Mission Demo that moves from flare HF blackout and Mars conjunction LOS through a vital anomaly, Local AI that states what happened, its hypothesized reason, and a citation check (supported / partial / not confirmed), second-crewmate care, recovery, and AOS restore, with an Earth-link panel of real offline windows, a device map separating sensors from crew-laptop local AI (target: Ollama 7B–8B Q4 on ~8 GB VRAM or ~32 GB RAM with citation-enforced Agentic RAG / GraphRAG), and nineteen in-app citations including all five official challenge resources; built with TypeScript, React, Tailwind, Recharts, Vitest, and Vercel (HyperFrames for video; optional Supabase receipt sync), it enables Earth-independent medical decision support in the spirit of NASA ExMC CDSS research for crews without a physician, creatively pairing honest citation verdicts, space-weather-driven LOS, and a two-crew apply story while staying honest that data is simulated, limits may be demo placeholders, and PULSE is not a medical device but complementary to CHeCS / ExMC—live at
